entries.title: DRAFT: P0017 dated primary-source status
entries.statement: DRAFT source audit as of 2026-10-10. P0017 asks for one universal C such that CP(mu)<=C for every dimension and every isotropic log-concave probability law. Isotropy means mean zero and covariance identity; CP is the variance-to-Euclidean-gradient-energy coefficient. Randomstrasse101 arXiv:2603.29571v1 Entry 13 Conjecture 30 gives the equivalent Cheeger bound c/sqrt(||Cov||op). arXiv:2610.05474v1 (4 October) and 2610.07728v1 (6 October) claim complete bounds. These source claims have not been fully independently audited here; current openness is UNKNOWN and the September attempted_unsolved label is historical.
assumptions: Dated source status is distinct from proof verification

entries.title: DRAFT refuted route: Gaussian diagonal Parseval for Appell polynomials
entries.statement: REFUTED DRAFT ROUTE, not an available identity: replacing Gaussian Hermite polynomials by centered Appell polynomials of a general isotropic log-concave law does not preserve diagonal Parseval. In particular the proposed equality Var(q1+q2)=E q1^2+E q2^2 fails for X=Exp(1)-1, q1=X and q2=(X^2-1)/2. The full variance requires their cross Gram term.
assumptions: Appell polynomials need not be orthogonal

entries.title: DRAFT: exact exponential Appell coefficient norms and Gram obstruction
entries.statement: DRAFT exact special case. For X=Y-1 with Y~Exp(1), define F_f(s)=E[f(X)exp(sX)]/E[exp(sX)]. The normalized tilt coefficient T_d f=F_f^(d)(0)/d! is E[f(X)q_d(Y)], where q_d(y)=y^d/d!-y^(d-1)/(d-1)! for d>=1. Its squared L2 operator norm is binomial(2d-2,d-1), attained by the normalized representer; its all-degree exponential rate is 2. Scalar cumulants of order m>=2 equal (m-1)!. Moreover q1=X, q2=(X^2-1)/2 have Gram entries 1, 2 and cross entry 1. Thus Var(q1+q2)=5, a diagonal sum gives 3, and E|(q1+q2)prime|^2=2. This does not prove a tensor bound for general laws.
assumptions: mu is not a regular smooth strongly log-concave law

entries.title: DRAFT refuted route: arbitrary tilts inherit initial isotropy
entries.statement: REFUTED DRAFT ROUTE: original isotropy of a log-concave law does not bound the covariance or Poincare constant of every normalized linear or Gaussian-damped tilt by a universal multiple of the original covariance. Log-concavity persists while covariance changes. A bound on the covariance of the current law, or a process-specific averaged estimate with its probability law and time range, is needed.
assumptions: No assertion about a specific localization process average

entries.title: DRAFT: exact exponential tilted covariance obstruction
entries.statement: DRAFT independently checked special case. For X=Exp(1)-1, the normalized linear tilt exp(sx), s<1, has mean s/(1-s), variance (1-s)^(-2), and CP at least that variance by the linear test. For t>0, the normalized tilt exp((1-t)x-tx^2/2) has variance (1-2/pi)/t: X+1 becomes half-normal with precision t. These laws are log-concave, and both variances can be arbitrarily large compared with the original variance 1. These deterministic examples do not refute KLS normalized with the current covariance, or an averaged localization estimate.

entries.title: DRAFT: posterior curvature yields non-strict Dirichlet contraction
entries.statement: DRAFT conditional deduction. Let X~mu be log-concave, G~N(0,I) independent, t>0, Y=X+sqrt(t)G, nu_t=Law(Y), and T_t f(y)=E[f(X)|Y=y]. For a law rho, D_rho(g)=integral |grad g|^2 d rho. For regular mu and finite-energy f, grad_y T_t f=Cov(f,X|Y=y)/t. The posterior curvature is at least 1/t, giving Cov(X|Y=y)<=tI and Var(f|Y=y)<=t E[|grad f|^2|Y=y]. Cauchy-Schwarz and averaging imply D_nu_t(T_t f)<=D_mu(f). Extension beyond regular laws needs the appropriate Sobolev approximation. This argument gives coefficient 1 and supplies no uniform strict margin.
assumptions: Begin with regular smooth log-concave mu
Finite gradient energy and justified conditional differentiation

entries.title: DRAFT: the strict averaged posterior bridge retains the KLS gap
entries.statement: DRAFT conditional equivalence, attributed to w357 and independently audited by w358. Let X~mu be centered, isotropic and log-concave, let G~N(0,I) be independent, Y=X+sqrt(t)G, nu_t=Law(Y), T_t f(y)=E[f(X)|Y=y], and D_rho(g)=integral |grad g|^2 d rho. Write Q_t(mu)=sup_f D_nu_t(T_t f)/D_mu(f) over Sobolev functions with positive finite energy. For log-concave mu with finite K=CP(mu), fixed t>0 and Q_t(mu)<=q<1 for every Sobolev f imply K<=t(1+q)/(1-q), by total variance and CP(mu*Gaussian_t)<=K+t. Conversely K<=C gives D(T_t f)<=Var_mu(f)/t<=C D_mu(f)/t; t=2C gives q=1/2. Thus a dimension-uniform strict posterior Dirichlet contraction at some fixed noise level is equivalent to a dimension-free KLS bound. Its nonlinear averaged gap remains unproved in this campaign packet. The unweighted MMSE covariance average cannot be substituted into an energy-weighted expectation.
assumptions: One fixed numerical t and q uniform over dimensions and laws
Uniform regular approximation for the full target

entries.title: DRAFT: exponential tail constrains a posterior contraction coefficient
entries.statement: DRAFT independently checked special-case derivation (w359 KEEP). For centered isotropic X=Exp(1)-1 observed through independent Gaussian noise of variance t>0, let Y=X+sqrt(t)G with independent G~N(0,1), nu_t=Law(Y), T_t f(y)=E[f(X)|Y=y], and D_rho(g)=integral |gprime|^2 d rho. Test f_a(x)=exp(a x), 0<a<1/2. A positive-tail calculation gives liminf as a increases to 1/2 of D_nu_t(T_t f_a)/D_mu(f_a)>=exp(-t/4). Hence any all-function coefficient q(t) must be at least exp(-t/4). At t=1 the explicit a=49/100 test has ratio greater than 7/10, using only the tail y>=5 in the untranslated observation coordinates. The exact Gaussian affine coefficient 1/4 at t=1 cannot hold for this law. This does not refute existence of some q<1.
assumptions: Translation to centered X preserves the ratio
Sobolev approximation needed if the initial test class is bounded

relations.rationale: Attach dated primary verification to the exact historical P0017 problem, preserving its unverified current-status caveat.
The historical card proves only Gaussian Hermite Parseval; this explicitly refuted extrapolation records the missing orthogonality premise.
At X=Exp(1)-1 the exact cross Gram term is 1: actual variance 5 differs from the proposed diagonal variance 3.
The initial isotropic variance is 1 but linear-tilt variance (1-s)^(-2) and quadratic-tilt variance (1-2/pi)/t diverge.
The conditional variance and covariance inequalities support the variance reduction; obtaining q<1 is an additional unproved premise.
This specific isotropic law imposes q(t)>=exp(-t/4) on any constants proposed for the full nonlinear bridge.
Exact exponential Appell Gram entries show why the Gaussian diagonal generator cannot be assumed for other log-concave laws.
